BiblicalUsage: Abel-keramim — the plain of the vineyards — is named once, in Judges 11:33, as the far end of Jephthah's pursuit: he smote the Ammonites 'from Aroer, even till thou come to Minnith, even twenty cities, and unto the plain of the vineyards, with a very great slaughter.' It is the finish line of the victory.
TheologicalSignificance: One place-name, one victory, and then the shadow of Jephthah's vow falls over the chapter. I believe the plain of the vineyards reminds me that victories end and vows remain — and that a triumph won in God's strength can still be followed by a foolish promise made in my own.
